title: Research compendium for "Mapping the AI Research of China, the US and the EU: A Scientometric Analysis of Citation Shares within AI Subdisciplines (2020-2025)"
description:
Complete research compendium for a scientometric analysis of citation shares within AI subdisciplines, based on metadata for 1,986,659 AI-related publications retrieved from OpenAlex for 2020-2025.

What the study does. It builds a data-driven map of AI research and then measures where each of China, the United States and the EU-27 holds influence within it. Subdisciplines are identified with a semi-supervised, hierarchical topic model: documents are embedded with SPECTER, deliberately over-segmented by K-Means at high granularity, and consolidated by an expert into interpretable units, iterated across three levels. The resulting taxonomy comprises 5 domains, 31 fields and 106 research fronts. Research impact is operationalized as the fractional citation sum - a work's citations split among the countries that produced it, in proportion to its authors' institutional shares - and decomposed across every cluster of that taxonomy.

External validation. Because the taxonomy is partly the product of expert judgement, it is tested from outside with a document-intrusion protocol adapted from the "reading tea leaves" paradigm of Chang et al. (2009): a language model is shown four genuine members of a cluster plus one intruder from a different cluster at the same level, with no labels or hints, and must identify the intruder. Detection accuracy is the coherence signal. Run at 1,000 trials per hierarchy level - 3,000 trials in total - accuracy rises monotonically with granularity: 40.5% at the macro level, 64.7% at the meso level and 77.8% at the micro level, against a 20% random baseline. The complete record of every trial is deposited here.

Contents. The full pipeline as seven numbered stages (keyword construction, OpenAlex retrieval, quality control, hierarchical topic modeling, impact analysis, visualization, and LLM-based cluster validation as an installable and tested Python package); the manifests, per-trial records, transcripts and run logs for all 3,000 validation trials; the article's Supplementary Information giving bloc citation shares for every cluster at all three hierarchy levels as PDF and CSV; and the manuscript sources, figures and bibliography.

The 20 GB labelled corpus is deposited as a separate data record; see data/README.md for its schema and provenance.
